html:
The heartbeat of an ice shelf. The sound in this video comes from the Ross Ice Shelf, Antarctica’s best-known ice shelf. Put simply, an ice shelf is an enormous slab of floating ice, and this one is roughly the size of France.

How can ice floating on the sea make such an otherworldly sound? The answer, surprisingly, is the wind: it sets this France-sized slab of ice vibrating. Some “bored” scientists noticed the sound and set about studying it, and found that its tones appear to be linked to global warming. They now plan to keep taking the ice shelf’s “cardiogram.”

Shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
